title: Interface demo: Introducing Yourself

Introduce yourself with a field, a concrete detail and a personal touch.

sections.title: Warm-up
sections.content: Think of the last time you introduced yourself to a group. What did you say first?

sections.title: First day, new team
sections.content:
Hi everyone, I'm Lena. I've just joined the product team from a small design studio in Tbilisi, so this is all a bit new to me.

Most of my work so far has been about making complicated things feel simple — onboarding screens, checkout flows, **that kind of thing**.

Outside work, I'm slowly learning to bake proper sourdough. It's going about as well as you'd expect. I'm really looking forward to working with you all.

evidenceSpans.text: It's going about as well as you'd expect.
I've just joined the product team

sections.title: Useful chunks
sections.content:
- **I've just joined…** — I've just joined the product team.
- **most of my work so far** — Most of my work so far has been about onboarding.
- **that kind of thing** — Checkout flows, sign-up forms, that kind of thing.

sections.title: Look forward to + -ing
sections.content: In *look forward to*, **to** is a preposition, so it is followed by a noun or an *-ing* form: *I'm looking forward to working with you.*

sections.title: Marco at a meetup
sections.content: Listen to Marco introducing himself at a meetup.
sections.transcript:
Hey, I'm Marco. I moved here about a year ago for work — I'm a data analyst at a logistics company, which is less boring than it sounds, I promise.

Honestly, I came tonight because I don't know many people outside the office yet.

evidenceSpans.text: I don't know many people outside the office yet

sections.title: Linking sounds
sections.content: Notice how *just joined* and *a bit new* link together in fast speech.

tasks.prompt: Which reply sounds most natural when someone says “So, what do you do?”

options.text: I am working as a marketing specialist since three years.
I work in marketing — I look after our social media.
My profession is marketing.

tasks.feedback: Natural speakers often give the field first, then one concrete detail.
tutorRules: Do not reveal the answer before the first attempt.

options.text: To show she is an expert baker.
To add a light, personal detail that makes her easier to talk to.
Because the team asked about her hobbies.

tasks.feedback: The self-deprecating line shows she isn’t boasting — it invites conversation.
tutorRules: Do not reveal the answer before the first attempt.

tasks.prompt: Which TWO things does Lena tell the team about her work?

options.text: She has just joined the product team.
She manages the design studio.
She makes complicated things feel simple.
She teaches baking.

tasks.feedback: She mentions her new team and the focus of her past work.
tutorRules: Do not reveal the answer before the first attempt.

tasks.prompt: Complete the chunk: “Checkout flows, sign-up forms, that ____ of thing.” Type the missing word.
tasks.feedback: “That kind of thing” (or “that sort of thing”) closes a list informally.
tutorRules: Do not reveal the answer before the first attempt.

tasks.prompt: I'm really looking forward ___ with you all. (work)
tasks.feedback: After “look forward to”, use the -ing form.

tasks.prompt: We've been looking forward ___ ___ the new team. (meet)
tasks.feedback: “to” is a preposition here, so the verb takes -ing.
